database_summary: Analytical heterogeneous dataset combining weekly retail sales, cleaned sales, customer activity and events (shopping cart users, events, page hierarchy, campaigns), cryptocurrency member/transaction/price data, interest metrics/maps, and detailed vegetable transaction/wholesale/loss/category tables. Mix of event-level tables (transactions, events), dimensional/descriptive tables (members, regions, page hierarchy, interest_map, veg_cat), and aggregated fact tables (weekly_sales, cleaned_weekly_sales, interest_metrics). Many tables use textual date fields and lack explicit surrogate primary keys in DDL. Several joins (e.g., cookie_id -> member_id, region/region_id) are possible but may multiply rows due to event-level detail.)

accepted.name: cleaned_weekly_sales_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date_formatted AS week_date_formatted,
  week_date AS week_date,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  transactions AS transactions,
  sales AS sales,
  week_number AS week_number,
  month_number AS month_number,
  calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  age_band AS age_band,
  demographic AS demographic,
  avg_transaction AS avg_transaction
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
accepted.description: Normalized projection of cleaned_weekly_sales exposing canonical date parts and preserving all descriptive columns and measures. Parses/aliases primary date and keeps calendar_year/week_number/month_number for easy time-based grouping. Use when asking time-series or dimensional breakdowns of weekly sales. | Use for: time-series of sales/transactions by region/platform/segment/customer_type; monthly or weekly aggregates and growth calculations; demographic or age_band performance comparisons; average transaction analyses and segmentation

accepted.name: weekly_sales_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  transactions AS transactions,
  sales AS sales
FROM weekly_sales
accepted.description: Projection of weekly_sales preserving original raw week_date text and all dimension/measure columns. Use when working with the raw weekly_sales fact (pre-cleaning) or comparing raw vs cleaned datasets. | Use for: raw weekly sales trends; data quality comparisons with cleaned_weekly_sales; dimension-level aggregates on raw data

accepted.name: shopping_cart_user_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id AS visit_id,
  e.cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  u.user_id AS user_id,
  e.page_id AS page_id,
  p.page_name AS page_name,
  p.product_category AS product_category,
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  e.event_type AS event_type,
  e.sequence_number AS sequence_number,
  e.event_time AS event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p ON e.page_id = p.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_users u ON e.cookie_id = u.cookie_id
accepted.description: Denormalized event-level relation joining shopping_cart_events to shopping_cart_page_hierarchy and shopping_cart_users (via cookie_id) to provide event context (page, product) and user identifier. Useful for funnel, session, and event-sequence analyses. | Use for: session funnel analyses (page sequences leading to conversion); event counts by page_name or product_category; joining events to users for retention/cohort studies

accepted.name: bitcoin_member_transactions
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.txn_id AS txn_id,
  t.member_id AS member_id,
  m.first_name AS first_name,
  m.region AS region,
  t.ticker AS ticker,
  t.txn_date AS txn_date,
  t.txn_time AS txn_time,
  t.txn_type AS txn_type,
  t.quantity AS quantity,
  t.percentage_fee AS percentage_fee
FROM bitcoin_transactions t
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members m ON t.member_id = m.member_id
accepted.description: Event-level join of bitcoin_transactions to bitcoin_members to attach member attributes (first_name, region) to each transaction. Useful for member-level activity, geographic breakdowns, and linking to external user identifiers if available. | Use for: member-level crypto trading volume and fee analysis; geographic distribution of transactions; join to price series by ticker/date for P&L

accepted.name: interest_monthly_metrics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  month_year AS month_year,
  _month AS _month,
  _year AS _year,
  COUNT(interest_id) AS interest_id_count,
  AVG(composition) AS avg_composition,
  AVG(index_value) AS avg_index_value
FROM interest_metrics
GROUP BY month_year, _month, _year
accepted.description: Monthly aggregated interest metrics per month_year that summarizes count of interest_id observations and average index/composition values. Useful for trend detection and month-level comparisons across interests. | Use for: monthly trends in interest composition/index; seasonal comparisons across years; identifying months with many active interests

accepted.name: customer_transactions_by_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  COUNT(*) AS txn_count,
  SUM(txn_amount) AS total_txn_amount,
  MIN(txn_date) AS first_txn_date,
  MAX(txn_date) AS last_txn_date
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id
accepted.description: Customer-level aggregated transactions summarizing total txn_amount, count of transactions, first and last txn_date. Useful for customer lifetime, recency-frequency-monetary (RFM) analyses. | Use for: customer lifetime value and frequency analyses; recency and tenure cohorts; identifying high-value customers

accepted.name: bitcoin_prices_clean
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker AS ticker,
  market_date AS market_date,
  price AS price,
  open AS open,
  high AS high,
  low AS low,
  volume AS volume,
  change AS change
FROM bitcoin_prices
accepted.description: Projection of bitcoin_prices keeping raw textual fields and numeric price/open/high/low. Leaves volume and change as-is (text) but exposes the core price series for joins. Use before time alignment with transaction dates. | Use for: time-series price joins with bitcoin_transactions; daily OHLC analyses; cleaning volume/change into numeric measures downstream

accepted.name: veg_transactions_with_category
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  v."index" AS "index",
  v.txn_date AS txn_date,
  v.txn_time AS txn_time,
  v.item_code AS item_code,
  c.item_name AS item_name,
  c.category_code AS category_code,
  c.category_name AS category_name,
  v."qty_sold(kg)" AS "qty_sold(kg)",
  v."unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" AS "unit_selling_px_rmb/kg",
  l."loss_rate_%" AS "loss_rate_%",
  v."sale/return" AS "sale/return",
  v."discount(%)" AS "discount(%)",
  v.day_of_week AS day_of_week
FROM veg_txn_df v
LEFT JOIN veg_cat c ON v.item_code = c.item_code
LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df l ON v.item_code = l.item_code
accepted.description: Joins veg_txn_df to veg_cat and veg_loss_rate_df (by item_code) to provide item name, category, and loss rate alongside each transaction. Useful for margin, category-level sales, and loss-adjusted analyses. | Use for: category-level sales and quantity sold; loss-rate adjusted revenue estimates; price and discount impact analyses by category

accepted.name: shopping_campaign_active_windows
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  campaign_id AS campaign_id,
  products AS products,
  campaign_name AS campaign_name,
  start_date AS start_date,
  end_date AS end_date
FROM shopping_cart_campaign_identifier
accepted.description: Campaign rows with start/end dates exposed for filtering to active campaigns in a dynamic query. Keeps campaign_id, campaign_name and product list. Use as a base for joining events or transactions to campaigns via date overlaps. | Use for: identify events/transactions that fall within campaign windows; campaign-level performance over their active period

accepted.name: shopping_cart_event_types
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_type AS event_type,
  event_name AS event_name
FROM shopping_cart_event_identifier
accepted.description: Simple projection of event type mappings to attach human-readable event_name to event_type. Use to decode event_type integers in event-level analyses. | Use for: map event_type to event_name for reporting; join to events to get descriptive event names
